name: ryu.bytebot
description: Drives a Bytebot desktop (https://github.com/bytebot-ai/bytebot) through `bytebotd`, its local HTTP daemon, as the SECOND provider of the swappable `computer.control` layer — the first thing that makes that layer actually swappable rather than merely marked selectable. READ THIS BEFORE SELECTING IT: bytebotd drives the desktop IT runs on, which in the shipped Bytebot product is a containerized Linux desktop, NOT the machine running Ryu. Selecting it re-points `computer.capture` / `computer.click` / `computer.type` / `computer.key` / `computer.scroll` away from your own screen (`ghost`, the declared default) and onto that desktop — the same remote-target relationship `browser.control` already has between the local Chromium sidecar and a hosted browser. It serves FIVE of the six canonical verbs: `computer.focus_app` is deliberately NOT bound, because bytebotd's `application` action takes a closed seven-value enum (firefox, 1password, thunderbird, vscode, terminal, desktop, directory) while the canonical verb takes a free-form app name, so any other name would be a schema-legal call that 400s. The app switch is still reachable natively as `bytebot.application`, whose own schema carries that enum so an illegal call cannot be composed. Requires no API key — bytebotd ships with no authentication at all, which is also why this plugin only ever addresses it over loopback. SECURITY, read before enabling: bytebotd ships with NO authentication — no auth middleware, permissive CORS — and this plugin reaches it at the fixed loopback port 9990. Its egress grant is `tool:http-egress:127.0.0.1`, which is HOST-scoped, not port-scoped: approving it grants reach to any service on loopback, not just bytebotd. Only enable this on a machine where you accept that an unauthenticated desktop-control daemon is running and reachable. TARGET: bytebotd drives the desktop IT runs on — in the shipped Bytebot product that is a containerized Linux desktop, NOT the machine running Ryu — so selecting this instead of `ghost` does not give you another way to drive your own computer.
